{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Re-load the data
file_path = '/home/musel/Github/research_agent/data/sales.csv'
data = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Convert revenue from string to float, handling commas
data['revenue'] = data['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Remove QA orders (revenue == 999999.99)
qa_mask = data['revenue'] == 999999.99
print(f"Number of QA orders removed: {qa_mask.sum()}")
data = data[~qa_mask]

# Correct the population: only orders with status == 'completed' AND converted == 1
completed_data = data[(data['status'] == 'completed') & (data['converted'] == 1)]

# Check that the contract's population is now valid
print(f"Number of orders in the contract's population (converted == 1): {data[data['converted'] == 1].shape[0]}")
print(f"Number of orders in the corrected population (status == 'completed' and converted == 1): {len(completed_data)}")

# Verify the contract's premise: 'converted = 1' means completed checkout
# But we found 21 orders where converted == 1 but status == 'refunded'
conversion_mismatch = data[(data['converted'] == 1) & (data['status'] == 'refunded')]
print(f"Number of orders where converted == 1 but status == 'refunded': {len(conversion_mismatch)}")

# Print the actual population used
print("\nFinal population (status == 'completed' and converted == 1):\n", completed_data[['channel', 'customer_segment', 'revenue']].head())"}
